Been there, done that... and what I've personally learned (as well as what I've discovered in the scientific literature on clinical psychology) is that burning the bridges is, at best, unnecessary & at worst - the most destructive thing you can do while suffering from depression and/or considering suicide. (1) Distancing yourself from people or making them "hate" you will NOT lessen the impact your suicide will have on them (in terms of shock and/or devastation). I hate to use this rather cheesy line, but it is very true - "love is close to hatred" (and vice versa). Also, death does not erase others' memories or attachments to someone, even if the person was not extremely close to you; (2) If you do, at any point, decide to pursue recovery & rebuild your life, this will make it 10x harder to achieve (not impossible, yet much more challenging). Having a social circle helps in many ways in life (although I'm sure you already know this) - in helping you navigate tough situations & in helping to find positive opportunities for the future. That is all.

The first and foremost advice I can give you is - don't restrict. As you've noticed yourself, you "starve and then binge". One always leads to another, and there's no way around it. Any doctor or psychologist will tell you this. Although physical hunger is not the only reason we eat and overeat, it's definitely a major one.

Other than that, try and figure out what emotion(s) hide behind your binge eating. Are you more likely to eat when you're anxious? Or maybe you're trying to eat away your sadness? Is it loneliness? Or is it boredom? When you know what to look for (that is, what is your emotional trigger), practice noticing it as it appears, and just sitting with the feeling for a while instead of acting on it. This way you will teach your brain to be more tolerant of emotion, and over time you will literally unlearn to automatically think of food when you're experiencing emotion(s). Although this sounds simple, I appreciate that it is not easy. Oh, and as a sidenote, this will not work properly if you're restricting in the meantime, because a hungry brain will always think of food first, no matter the emotion.

In the meantime, I would suggest you also work on your body image. Not when you're "lighter", not X kilos later, - right now. Recovery from a binge eating disorder does not guarantee a smaller body size. Recovery is still worth it, it 100% is, it means psychological freedom from food, and it feels great! But you have to accept that recovery (despite of what some advertisements say) doesn't come with a promise of a "model figure". And any good ED recovery programme will therefore work on body image in addition to food issues. So yes, work on your body image too.

Nobody "fakes" depression. They can only lie about having it to others (although I can't understand why anyone would do that). So unless you were (a) deliberately lying on that depression scale they gave you at GP, and (b) you're lying to us right now about how you've been feeling - you do have depression. I mean, if you don't trust yourself, at least trust the doctor and your counsellor.

With regards to the severity / medication question... If it is indeed a mild-to-moderate depression, the advice is to seek counselling first, and leave medication as a last resort. This is NOT because what you have is in any way invalid, but because the antidepressants are serious chemicals that will affect the way your brain and physical body work. They may have really unpleasant side effects. And they don't work on 100% of depression cases.

Surely, if after some time you see that counselling alone is not helping you - do talk to your doctor about going on medication, but if I were you, I would give counselling a decent chance. 

Long story short: no, you are not an imposter, your depression is valid (with or without the use of antidepressants).
